high.title: [Microsoft Expands AI Compute Capacity Rental — Boosting Infrastructure Demand; Hon Hai, Quanta Among Beneficiaries]
high.summary:
According to Business Insider, Microsoft — ahead of its Q4 FY2026 earnings release on July 29 — is reportedly in talks to rent AI computing capacity from Amazon and Google, signaling that its own planned capital expenditure of USD 190 billion for the year is insufficient to meet surging AI workload demand. This is a significant data point: despite record-breaking capex commitments, hyperscalers are still capacity-constrained, undermining the AI bubble narrative and reinforcing the structural demand thesis for AI infrastructure.

For Taiwan's supply chain, the implications are directly bullish. Hon Hai (2317), Quanta, Wistron, Wiwynn, and Inventec — all key AI server manufacturers — stand to benefit from continued and potentially accelerating order flow as Amazon and Google respond to rental demand by expanding their own infrastructure build-outs. Microsoft's earnings release will be closely watched for any upward revision to FY2027 capex guidance, which would serve as a further catalyst. Investors in Taiwan's AI server supply chain should maintain overweight positions, with Hon Hai as the primary proxy.

high.title: [Nvidia Backs OpenAI's Super Data Center; Hon Hai Shipments Expected to Surge]
high.summary:
The Wall Street Journal reports that Nvidia is set to provide USD 250 billion in financing guarantees to help OpenAI lease a 10GW data center being developed by SoftBank in southern Ohio, as part of what could become the largest AI data center project in history with a total investment exceeding USD 500 billion. Nvidia's backing is critical because OpenAI — as a private, unprofitable entity — cannot obtain investment-grade credit ratings independently, making the guarantee essential to securing favorable debt terms for SoftBank.

Hon Hai (2317), as a key strategic partner to both OpenAI and SoftBank, is widely expected by industry sources to serve as the primary hardware supplier for AI servers and data center infrastructure, potentially triggering a significant step-up in shipment volumes. This represents a landmark demand event for Taiwan's AI hardware ecosystem. The scale of this project — USD 500 billion+ — dwarfs previous announcements and could sustain multi-year order visibility for Hon Hai. This is a high-conviction positive catalyst; investors should treat any pullback in Hon Hai shares as a buying opportunity.

high.title: Hon Hai Subsidiary Foxconn Industrial Internet (FII) Launches Share Buyback of Up to RMB 2 Billion to Defend Share Price
high.summary:
Hon Hai (2317) announced that its A-share listed subsidiary Foxconn Industrial Internet (FII / 工業富聯) has approved a share buyback program of RMB 1–2 billion (approximately USD 138–276 million) via centralized competitive bidding, with a repurchase price capped at RMB 103 per share, to be completed within three months. The buyback was triggered after FII's stock declined more than 20% over 20 consecutive trading sessions, prompting the board to act in defense of shareholder value. FII cited strong fundamental confidence: its H1 2026 net profit is estimated at RMB 23.4–24.4 billion, up 93–101% year-on-year, driven by AI server demand — with AI-related CSP revenue surging over 230% YoY. For Hon Hai investors, this is a meaningful signal: FII's aggressive buyback underscores management's conviction in the AI infrastructure supercycle, while also highlighting near-term share price volatility risk in its China-listed entity. The magnitude of profit growth in cloud/AI segments reinforces Hon Hai's strategic positioning as a key beneficiary of global AI capex expansion, which has direct read-through implications for Hon Hai's own valuation on the Taiwan Stock Exchange.

---

high.title: [Taiwan Stock Market: Foreign Investors Turn Net Buyers; Market Awaits Fed FOMC Rate Decision]
high.summary: Taiwan's equity market experienced extreme intraday volatility on July 27, initially dropping sharply following weakness in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index and Taiwan futures during Friday's overnight session. However, the index staged a remarkable V-shaped recovery after foreign investors (外資) reversed course to become net buyers of NT$8.04 billion, attracting additional short-term opportunistic buying. The TAIEX closed marginally lower by 20 points at 43,634, with turnover at NT$747.6 billion in a "price-down, volume-down" configuration.

high.title: Taiwan Stock Market Rebounds on Three Major Buying Forces; FX Market Eyes Three Key Factors This Week
high.summary:
Taiwan's equity market experienced significant intraday volatility on July 27, plunging as much as 685 points to 42,969 — breaching the key 43,000 level — before recovering sharply. The rebound was driven by coordinated buying from three major investor groups: foreign institutions (外資), life insurers (壽險), and dominant retail operators (主力), with buying concentrated in index heavyweights including TSMC. The market ultimately recovered 664 points from its intraday low.

On the currency front, the New Taiwan Dollar initially weakened but reversed course in the afternoon session as foreign capital inflows resumed, closing at 32.305, appreciating 5.3 cents (+0.16%) against the USD on volume of USD 2.072 billion. Notably, foreign investors turned net buyers of Taiwan equities at NT$8.04 billion — a significant positive signal after prior selling pressure.

high.title: [Kumamoto Earthquake: TSMC Impact Limited — Ministry of Economic Affairs Reports Taiwan Manufacturers Unaffected]
high.summary:
A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck Kumamoto, Japan on July 28, prompting TSMC's JASM fab to immediately evacuate personnel as a precautionary measure. TSMC confirmed by evening that all staff are safe, structural inspections cleared the facility as sound, and production lines are gradually resuming. Detailed damage assessments remain ongoing. JASM's second fab, currently under construction, has partially suspended work due to safety concerns, though the construction site itself was reported unaffected.

From a market impact perspective, the JASM Phase 1 facility produces mature nodes (28/22/16/12nm) at approximately 20,000 wafers/month, representing only ~2.6% of TSMC's total capacity and an estimated ~1% of 2026 revenues. Institutional analysts therefore view the financial impact as limited. However, TSMC's ADR fell approximately 3.8% in early U.S. trading on Tuesday, suggesting near-term sentiment risk. Taiwan-invested manufacturers in Kumamoto — including Advantech, Delta Electronics, and others — also reported no personnel casualties or operational disruptions. Investors should monitor aftershock developments and the timeline for full JASM production restoration.

high.title: [Unimicron Aggressively Raises 2026 Capex to NT$53.7 Billion — Up Over 57%]
high.summary:
Unimicron Technology (3037), Taiwan's leading IC substrate (載板) manufacturer, announced a major upward revision to its 2026 capital expenditure budget. The board approved an increase of approximately NT$19.7 billion on top of the original NT$34.0 billion plan, bringing the total to approximately NT$53.7 billion — a surge of over 57%. Additionally, the board approved a further NT$17.6 billion increase in long lead-time equipment pre-orders, with planned investment of ~NT$37.3 billion funded via internal cash and bank financing.

The stated purpose is to construct new facilities and upgrade process capabilities in line with customer demand. This is a significant signal of robust downstream demand for IC substrates, likely driven by AI server, HPC, and advanced packaging trends. The aggressive capex revision suggests strong customer pull — potentially from hyperscalers and chip designers — and reinforces the bullish outlook for Taiwan's semiconductor supply chain. For fund managers, this may also prompt scrutiny of Unimicron's balance sheet leverage and financing costs given the scale of the commitment.

high.title: TSMC: JASM Personnel and Facilities Confirmed Safe After Kumamoto Major Earthquake, Operations Gradually Resuming
high.summary:
A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck Kumamoto, Japan at approximately 4:27 PM local time on July 28, triggering TSMC's Japan subsidiary JASM to activate internal safety protocols and immediately evacuate personnel. The maximum ground motion recorded at the JASM fab site was intensity level 5. TSMC confirmed in an evening statement that all personnel are safe, post-earthquake structural damage inspections of fab buildings have been completed with structures confirmed sound, and production lines are gradually resuming. Detailed inspections and impact assessments remain ongoing. The under-construction Fab 2 site was not directly affected; however, some construction work has been temporarily suspended as a precautionary measure against potential aftershocks. JASM Fab 1 entered mass production in late 2024 using specialty process nodes, while the upcoming Fab 2 is planned to deploy 3nm technology with volume production targeted for 2028. Near-term market implication: production disruption risk appears contained based on current disclosures, but investors should monitor aftershock developments and any updates on equipment re-qualification timelines, which could affect near-term wafer output from the Kumamoto site.

---

high.title: Global Chip Stocks Plunge — Taiwan Stock Market Crashes 2,030 Points; Three Signals to Watch for a Bottom
high.summary: Taiwan's equity market suffered its third-largest single-day point decline in history on July 28, plunging 2,030 points (4.65%) to close at 41,603 — breaching both the 42,000 psychological level and the prior near-term low of 41,967. The catalyst was a reported major breakthrough by mainland China's semiconductor industry in DUV lithography technology, which triggered a 2.2% decline in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index overnight. The selloff was broad-based across Asia: Korea's KOSPI hit circuit breakers, falling 10.8%, while Japan's Nikkei dropped 3.8%. Trading volume on the Taiwan exchange surged 16.7% to NT$872.5 billion, though still well below July's average of NT$1.03 trillion. The FSC (金管會) again attempted to reassure investors, noting that listed company cumulative revenues through June reached NT$30.49 trillion (+35.96% YoY) and the market P/E stands at 31.78x. Institutional analysts warn the correction may not be over, with 40,000 as the next key support level. Three signals to monitor for a floor: TSMC and the broader index reclaiming their 5-day moving averages; foreign investors ceasing to expand net short positions in TAIEX futures; and margin loan balances continuing to decline. **Market implication:** The technical breakdown is severe and margin-call cascades remain a near-term risk. Fund managers should monitor FSC intervention posture and foreign futures positioning closely before re-engaging.

high.title: Semiconductor and Memory Stocks — Taiwan Market's Hardest Hit; TSMC, Nanya Tech Combined Market Cap Shrinks by NT$3 Trillion in One Day
high.summary: The semiconductor and memory sectors bore the brunt of the July 28 selloff, with combined market capitalization eroding by approximately NT$3 trillion in a single session. The "semiconductor triad" — TSMC (2330), MediaTek (2454), and ASE Technology (3711) — collectively shed NT$2.63 trillion in market cap. TSMC fell NT$70 to close at NT$2,280, wiping out NT$1.81 trillion in market value. MediaTek hit its daily limit-down of NT$3,315 (-NT$365), losing NT$585.4 billion in cap. ASE dropped NT$54 to NT$554, shedding NT$241.4 billion. Memory stocks were similarly devastated: Nanya Technology (2408) fell NT$43.5 to NT$392.5 (-NT$150 billion in cap), Winbond (2344) lost NT$16 closing at NT$144 (-NT$72 billion), and Phison (8299) dropped NT$170 to NT$1,650. Including a broader basket of memory-related names, the sector lost approximately NT$300 billion. **Market implication:** The scale of single-day market cap destruction is extraordinary and reflects forced deleveraging rather than purely fundamental repricing. For life insurers and institutional holders with large unrealized gains in TSMC and semiconductor names, mark-to-market equity losses will be material. Watch for potential portfolio rebalancing flows in the days ahead.

medium.title: [Five Industries Set to Benefit from US Tariff Preferential Treatment; Taiwan Gains 10% Non-Stacked Rate Advantage]
medium.summary: Taiwan's achievement of a 10% non-stacked tariff treatment from the US — compared to significantly higher rates applied to China and other Asian competitors — is opening order-diversion opportunities across five key export sectors: bicycles, machine tools & machinery, hand tools & plumbing hardware, petrochemicals & textiles, and medical devices. Machine tool makers are already reporting tangible results, with Cheng Tai Group (1583), Asia Pacific Elite Corp (1530), Tongtai (4526), Kao Fong (4510), Hiwin (2049), and Taiwan Takisawa (4583) reporting order growth of 15–40% compared to early 2026. US distributors are responding positively with restocking orders. While these are mid-cap industrials rather than the fund's primary focus, the macro signal is important: Taiwan's improved tariff positioning is a structural tailwind for export competitiveness that could support broader economic momentum and benefit sectors beyond tech.

medium.title: [Nvidia Raises GPU Prices Again by Up to 30%; Gigabyte, Leadtek and Board Makers to Benefit]
medium.summary: Nvidia has issued a third round of GPU price increases in 2026 (following hikes in January and May), raising graphics card prices by approximately 20–30% due to persistent DRAM cost inflation. Samsung's Q3 DRAM contract prices are reportedly rising 20%, with potential read-through for Taiwan's Nanya Technology (2408) and Winbond (2344). Taiwan add-in board manufacturers — ASUS (2357), MSI (2377), Gigabyte (2376), and Leadtek (2465) — are expected to benefit from improved ASPs and margin tailwinds. Channel distributors are reportedly hoarding inventory in anticipation of further price increases. While this is a positive near-term margin story for board makers, investors should monitor whether demand elasticity becomes a constraint if pricing rises too aggressively.

medium.title: Taiwan Cement (Taiwan Cement / 台泥) Launches European Listing Plan "Project Arcadia" — Chairman Chang An-ping Aims to Redefine Low-Carbon Building Materials Industry
medium.summary: Taiwan Cement (1101) Chairman Chang An-ping and President Cheng Yao-hui held a video conference with international investment banks and advisors on July 27 to formally kick off "Project Arcadia," the company's European capital market listing initiative. Taiwan Cement first disclosed its European listing consideration at its 80th anniversary event in May 2026. The plan involves repositioning the company not merely as a cement producer, but as a future-oriented low-carbon building materials ecosystem player, leveraging technology and material innovation. The proposal is expected to be submitted for board approval at the August board meeting. While Taiwan Cement is not a core holding for life insurance or financial-sector-focused funds, its overseas listing ambition is notable for Taiwan-listed company investors as it signals increasing appetite among traditional industry leaders to access international capital markets and ESG-oriented investor bases in Europe.

medium.title: Foxconn Industrial Internet Proposes Over RMB 1 Billion Share Repurchase via Competitive Bidding
medium.summary: This article is a companion/earlier report to the Article 4 Hon Hai/FII buyback story, confirming that Foxconn Industrial Internet (富士康工業互聯) has formally decided to repurchase shares via centralized competitive bidding within three months, with a total buyback budget of RMB 1–2 billion and a per-share price cap of RMB 103. The rationale is consistent: a 20%+ cumulative decline over 20 trading days triggered the buyback threshold. This corroborates the signal from Article 4 and reinforces the view that Hon Hai's ecosystem companies are actively managing market valuations amid broader market volatility, while maintaining confidence in AI-driven earnings growth.

medium.title: [International Oil Prices Plunge as Middle East Supply Threat Eases]
medium.summary: WTI crude fell $6.70/barrel (-7.5%) to $82.61, and Brent crude dropped $8.42/barrel (-8.7%) to $88.36, after the US suspended daily airstrikes on Iran and President Trump indicated progress in US-Iran negotiations. **Relevance:** The sharp oil price decline significantly reduces near-term global inflation pressure, which may provide the Fed room to maintain or ease its stance at the July 30 FOMC — a positive signal for risk assets including Taiwan equities. Additionally, lower energy costs benefit Taiwan's energy-intensive manufacturers and reduce imported inflation, giving the CBC greater policy flexibility.

medium.title: Hon Hai and Delta Electronics: Four Warrants in Focus
medium.summary: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang reaffirmed that Vera Rubin chips have entered mass production, lifting outlook for Taiwan's AI supply chain, particularly Hon Hai (2317) and Delta Electronics (2308). Hon Hai reported record-high Q2 revenue, beating market expectations, and is positioned as the dominant AI server assembly leader with over 40% market share across GPU and ASIC segments. Analysts project Hon Hai's Q3 operating performance will show double-digit sequential and year-over-year growth, supported by AI rack shipments, CPO switch ramp-up in H2, and new EV model deliveries to Australia and New Zealand. Delta Electronics is expected to benefit from Q3 price adjustments and strong AI server power supply orders. Both names remain high-conviction AI infrastructure plays within the Taiwan listed universe.

medium.title: AI Server ODM Firms Deploy Capital Aggressively: Quanta Acquires AUO Factory for NT$19.7 Billion
medium.summary: Taiwan's three major ODM manufacturers — Quanta (2382), Wistron (3231), and Inventec (2356) — are aggressively expanding AI server production capacity through major real estate and facility investments. Quanta announced the acquisition of AUO's Taoyuan Huaya Science Park facility for NT$19.7 billion (approximately 19,700 ping of land and 49,300 ping of building space), which will be converted into new AI server production lines. Wistron acquired new property in California for USD 121 million (NT$3.922 billion), while Inventec is building new facilities in Taoyuan and Thailand and expanding in Texas, with total committed capex of NT$18.131 billion. The AUO divestiture generates a disposal gain of NT$13.39 billion for AUO, supporting its strategic pivot toward an asset-light operating model. This wave of capex signals robust long-term AI server demand visibility and represents a structural re-allocation of industrial real estate across Taiwan's tech ecosystem.

medium.title: [Amazon Expands Satellite Launch Plans — Taiwanese Supply Chain (Shengtai, Huatong, ITEQ, etc.) to Benefit from New Orders]
medium.summary:
Amazon has filed with the FCC to launch an additional 5,105 direct-to-device (D2D) satellites on top of its existing 3,232-satellite Kuiper broadband constellation, putting it in direct competition with SpaceX's Starlink Mobile. Launches are planned to begin in 2028. Institutional investors expect Taiwanese supply chain companies — including Shengtai Technology (3491), Huatong (2313), ITEQ (2383), Yaohwa (2367), and Qisda (6285) — to receive a new wave of orders in RF components, PCBs, copper-clad laminates, and thermal management solutions. Given the inherently short lifespan and large-scale deployment nature of LEO satellites, sustained demand for these components is expected to remain elevated as global operators continue expanding their constellations.

---

medium.title: Kumamoto Earthquake Disrupts TSMC JASM Operations — Company Issues Latest Statement
medium.summary: This article provides TSMC's formal response to media inquiries regarding the impact of the July 28 Kumamoto earthquake on JASM operations. The company confirmed immediate personnel evacuation under internal safety protocols, with all staff confirmed safe. Post-earthquake structural inspections have cleared buildings as structurally sound, and operations are progressively resuming. Some construction work at the expansion site has been paused due to potential aftershock risks. This article is substantively consistent with Article 1 but represents TSMC's official on-record response to press queries, adding slight disclosure context for investor relations purposes.

medium.title: ADATA Reports Record H1 EPS of NT$62.46; Q2 Net Income Surpasses NT$10 Billion for First Time; Approves NT$18 Interim Dividend
medium.summary: Memory module maker ADATA Technology (3260) reported a landmark Q2 net profit of NT$10.4 billion — its first-ever quarter exceeding the NT$10 billion threshold — representing a 9.1% QoQ increase and over tenfold YoY growth, with EPS of NT$32.39. H1 2026 net profit reached NT$19.94 billion (EPS: NT$62.46), up 13x YoY, already far surpassing any prior full-year result. Q2 revenue came in at NT$38.14 billion (+46.1% QoQ, +197.4% YoY) with gross margin at 42.1%. The board approved a first-ever interim cash dividend of NT$18 per share. Chairman Chen Li-pai cited tightening global memory supply driven by AI demand expansion as a key tailwind, expressing confidence in continued Q3 profit growth. This result signals strong AI-driven memory demand momentum, relevant for investors tracking Taiwan's semiconductor supply chain.

medium.title: The Leveraged ETF "Surgery" — When Does the Deleveraging Stop?
medium.summary: Moore Investment Advisory's CIO Guo Zherong argues that the 2,030-point crash is likely the beginning — not the end — of a deleveraging cycle, rather than a fundamental AI bubble burst. He draws a parallel with Korea, where the FSC mandated higher margin requirements on leveraged ETFs (2x products) for Samsung and SK Hynix through July 31, triggering forced liquidations. Taiwan is undergoing a similar "leveraged ETF surgery." From a technical standpoint, the market is exhibiting a pattern of lower highs and lower lows, with no clear near-term support visible on charts. Brokers have reportedly issued margin call warnings, with a further decline of ~400 points (to ~41,250) likely to trigger a wave of forced liquidations. The TAIEX could test the 40,000 level if global markets continue to deteriorate. **Relevance:** The margin call threshold at ~41,250 is a critical near-term risk level for fund managers to monitor; forced selling from retail leverage could amplify downside volatility independent of fundamental developments.

medium.title: Hon Hai and Wistron — Warrant Buying Opportunities Amid Volatility
medium.summary: Despite broad market turbulence, foreign investors and domestic investment trusts (投信) have been simultaneously net buyers in select fundamentally sound stocks, notably Hon Hai (2317) and Wistron (3231), both key AI server supply chain beneficiaries. Hon Hai is scheduled to hold its investor conference on August 12, with earnings expected to beat consensus; its subsidiary Industrial Foxconn reported AI server revenue growth of 230% YoY in H1 2026. With GB300 rack shipments ramping and Rubin chip deliveries commencing, Hon Hai's full-year AI-related revenue is expected to sustain triple-digit growth. Hon Hai is also expanding U.S. manufacturing capacity, projected to surpass Mexico by end of 2024, while strengthening its thermal component vertical integration. **Relevance:** The concurrent buying by foreign investors and domestic funds in Hon Hai and Wistron amid broad selling provides a useful signal of institutional conviction in AI server supply chain names; this may be worth monitoring for re-entry positioning once broader deleveraging stabilizes.
